title: Get the Money Ready for OpenAI's Massive Order: Oracle Says Financing Is in Place

content_html:
Supplying OpenAI requires enormous amounts of capital, and Oracle wants to prove to the market that it is not short of money. On November 20 local time, the cloud provider said it had raised all the funds needed earlier this month to fulfill its contract with OpenAI, and that any further private talks with suppliers are merely nice-to-have extras, not necessary moves.

Abilene Is Already Training GPT-6 Astra

Beyond the funding being in place, engineering progress was also put on display to prove the deal is genuinely moving forward. The Abilene campus in Texas is the flagship project in the two parties’ AI infrastructure partnership and is now being used to train GPT-6 Astra, with the overall project nearing completion; the next gigawatt-scale project, Shackelford, has also secured all permits; delivery of NVIDIA Vera Rubin racks is proceeding as planned and is expected to be completed within the next few weeks.

FY2029 Target: $30 Billion in Free Cash Flow

The question capital markets care about most is when this asset-heavy approach will pay off. Oracle’s timetable is quite specific: positive free cash flow in the second half of FY2028, more than $30 billion (about RMB 200.8 billion) in free cash flow in FY2029, and from then on funding future growth with its own capital—no longer relying on external funding. The remarks are also intended to address outside doubts that its OpenAI orders depend on a financing cycle: although massive compute orders are attractive, whether the pay-first-and-get-paid-later model can work will depend on whether these fiscal years deliver.
